changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/5876-one-lookup-predicate.md`

- names `ObjectDataTable.tsx` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `computeLookupExpand` in `ObjectDataTable.tsx` carried its own `isLookup`, byte-identical to the exported `isLookupType` in `recordFields.tsx` after objectui#5692 pointed both at `@object-ui/core`'s `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`. Nothing kept them aligned: a future edit to either — a member added, the retirement gate moved — would have re-forked the `$expand` decision from the predicate whose docblock claims to drive it. `computeLookupExpand` now calls `isLookupType`, which gains its first production consumer, and the module no longer imports the shared family or the retirement gate at all.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `ObjectDataTable.tsx` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8253-export-tree-view-config.md`

- names `plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx` → `packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was wrong.** `tree` is a host-composition-only view type — ruled deliberate on objectui#5321, it is a member of neither `ObjectViewSchema.defaultViewType` nor `NamedListView.type`, so the branch runs only when a host passes a `views` prop. On that path a per-view `tree` block is read at four sites, and its only description anywhere was a module-local, non-exported `interface TreeConfig` inside `plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx`. The live host is the console: it stores view records and passes them as `views`, and its create-view dialog offers `tree`. So a real consumer wrote this block with no type to write it against, and a misspelled `parentFeild` was admitted by the views entry's `[key: string]: any`, stored, read by nobody and reported by nothing. Declared ≠ enforced on a surface a non-author re-writes.

### `.changeset/dashboard-expandable-family-convergence-5692.md`

- names `ObjectDataTable.tsx` → `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectDataTable.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `plugin-dashboard`'s two private copies of the reference-bearing field family now read `@object-ui/core`'s published `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` instead of restating it — `LOOKUP_TYPES` in `recordFields.tsx` and the inline disjunction inside `computeLookupExpand` in `ObjectDataTable.tsx`. Both carry the identity pin the already-converged consumers carry, so a member-identical private copy fails rather than quietly re-forking the table.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `a14fb23b3` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1600 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2189 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36335159815)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72c4b48780276d43d0830bf234284790c12fd872`

### ① Derived judgments

**Seam per block (read at head, no execution).**
- **`object-tree`: correct.**
  - The nonce is keyed on `dataObjectName`. That name is defined only for the `object` provider, and it is the object `find` names, whether the node spells it `objectName` or `data: { provider: 'object', object }`.
  - It subscribes on `dataSource ? dataObjectName : undefined`. That is exactly the arm that queries (`dataProvider === 'object' && dataSource`).
  - An inline array or the `value` provider yields `undefined`, so it never subscribes.
- **`object-pivot`: correct.**
  - Keyed on `schema.objectName`, gated by `fetchesForItself`. That gate is the effect's own fetch guard: a data source, an `objectName`, no `bind` rows and no authored `data`.
  - `ObjectPivotBlock`'s `ElementDataSourceGate` binds `dataSource: { object }` onto `objectName` before this component reads it.
- **`object-data-table`: correct.** Same gate as the pivot, and the key is the object `find` names.
- **Static data does not refetch.**
  - Authored `data` rows and `bind` rows compute `undefined`: no subscription, no refetch.
  - Pinned for authored rows in all three blocks and for the tree's `value` provider.
  - `bind` rows are not pinned. I accept them by reading, because the gate is the same expression as the effect guard.
- **No loop, no stale-closure problem.**
  - The nonce moves only on a bus event, and `find` emits no `onMutation`, so the effect cannot trigger itself.
  - Each effect keeps its existing `cancelled` / `isMounted` guard. A rapid second event re-runs the effect, and the superseded run's state writes are dropped.
  - The superseded request is not aborted (there is no AbortController). That is the existing objectui#10572 / #10623 shape (`ObjectMetricWidget`), not a defect of this PR.
- **`ObjectDataTable` drill-down: code correct, prose overclaims** (see Changesets).
  - `DrillDownDrawer`'s record list, and `ObjectChart`'s own drill drawer (which mounts `object-data-table` through `SchemaRenderer`), both re-read.
  - `RecordDetailDrawer` holds the clicked row as a snapshot and fetches nothing.
  - The `drillDown.report` arm of `DrillDownDrawer` renders `spec-report`, which has no reader.
- **Draw window untouched.**
  - The diff touches only the `@object-ui/react` import, one block above the fetch effect, and its dependency list. `objectTypesPending`, `enrich`, the columns memo and the drawer props are not touched.
  - Seat 4's branch (now `e8503d38be`) edits the `@object-ui/fields` import, `withheldCell`, `enrich` and the `RecordDetailDrawer` props. No overlap.
- The shape matches objectui#10572 / #10623: same hook, `dataChangeMatches`, no second channel, no remount.

**The double read on list-view trees: a real cost, not a correctness regression. Acceptable, and not a landing blocker.**
- **What happens.** On a bus event the tree reads once on its nonce, then again when ListView's own bus re-read hands down a fresh array.
- **What it costs.** One extra `find` per write to that object, capped at the non-grid row ceiling and with every expandable relation. The console's `useMutationInvalidationBridge` puts every dataSource write on the bus, so this happens on every write, not only on page actions.
- **What is pre-existing.** The 'Loading…' placeholder and the lost scroll happen on every tree refetch, because `setLoading(true)` swaps the table for the placeholder. On main a list-view tree already refetches when ListView's re-read lands.
- **What the head adds.** A possible second flash (rows, then 'Loading…', then rows) when read 1 lands before ListView's rows do.
- **Why subscribing is still right.** Gating host-fed rows out would make freshness depend on the host handing down a new array. AGENTS.md #10 forbids a provider from republishing an equal payload as a new object, so a compliant host would never move `data` for a write outside its projection (for example, a re-parented record).
- **Recommended follow-up card, not in this PR.** ObjectTree should keep its rows during a re-read, with a `RefreshIndicator` over them as `ObjectDataTable` has. That removes the flash and the scroll loss for every refetch. It matters more once objectui#10777 lands: a page action on a page holding a tree then flashes 'Loading…' in place of today's full remount.

**Pins: real driver, real event, real controls.**
- 13 cases in three files. Each renders through the real `SchemaRenderer` under `SchemaRendererProvider`, using the package's own `./index` registration.
- Each fires `notifyDataChanged` from `@object-ui/react`, the same source module the components import through the alias.
- The lit control is a bare `useDataInvalidation` `BusControl`, asserted at `1` in every case.
- The negatives are real: an unrelated object stays at 1 read, and authored rows and the `value` provider never query.
- In-place evidence: the same `table` node for the pivot and the table, a flipped expansion surviving in the tree, and the new value painted.
- The dev's legs are consistent with the source:
  - BASE: 10 red (tree 4, pivot 3, table 3), 3 controls green.
  - Ablation A2: exactly the pivot's 3 read-after-event cases red.
- Gaps, non-blocking: `bind` rows are not pinned, and the list-view double read is not pinned as a count.

**Census: can a stored page hold each unread row, and does it read on PageView's path?** `PageComponentSchema.type` is `PageComponentType` or an open string, so any registered key can be held.
- **`dashboard` dataset-bound widgets: do not gate.** Holdable, but they issue no query through PageView, because `DatasetWidget` gets `dataSource` only as a prop from `DashboardRenderer`. Removing the remount cannot make them staler. File the class (a) card and let the reader ride it. I agree with the dev.
- **`report` / `spec-report` over a dataset: gate.** Holdable. It reads `queryDataset` on mount, and its effect keys on `[signature]` only, so it goes stale once the remount goes. File it as a blocker of objectui#10519. I agree with A.
- **`record:activity`: does not gate.** It needs `useRecordContext` for its object and id, and PageView provides no record context.
- **`record:history`: does not gate.** Same as activity: record context only.
- **`record:line_items`: gate. The dev's Acceptance note 3 is wrong for this row.**
  - `LineItemsPanel` resolves `parentId = schema.parentId || schema.recordId || record?.recordId` and takes `dataSource` from `useSchemaContext`.
  - A stored page node with an authored `parentId` or `recordId` therefore reads `find(childObject)` on mount with no record context.
  - Under the letter of decision B it gates. Name it on the same blocker card as report/spec-report. Its reach is low, but it can be held and it reads.
- **`record:reference_rail`: does not gate.** Both `parentId` and `dataSource` come from the record context only.
- **A versus B: A, amended.**
  - The objectui#10519 blocker card carries report/spec-report and the authored-parent arm of `record:line_items`.
  - The dashboard dataset widgets go on an independent class (a) card.

**Changesets, sentence by sentence.**
- **`.changeset/10778-dashboard-bus-readers.md`.**
  - True: the title, the first paragraph's three sentences, the pivot-spelling sentence, and "Bound rows and authored `data` rows do not subscribe."
  - False: "and what every drill-down drawer lists records with, so those re-read too". A drill configured with `drillDown.report` (the metric and the pivot pass one) renders `spec-report`, which has no reader. The drawer a table row opens is a snapshot.
  - Replace the last paragraph's second sentence with: "The table is also what a `dashboard` block draws for a table widget over `{ provider: 'object' }` and what a drill-down drawer lists the underlying records with, so those re-read too. A drill that opens a report (`drillDown.report`) and the single-record drawer a table row opens do not re-read."
- **`.changeset/10778-tree-bus-reader.md`.**
  - True: the title, the first sentence, and both sentences of the last paragraph.
  - False as written: "Before, the tree refreshed after such a write only when its host remounted it". A `list-view` tree also refreshed on ListView's re-read. The card's own "Not affected" row says so, and so does this changeset's last paragraph.
  - Replace that sentence with: "Before, a tree that no host handed rows to refreshed after such a write only when its host remounted it, and `PageView` is about to stop doing that (objectui#10519)."
- There are no dated notes. Both frontmatters are well-formed single-package `patch` lines.

**PR body.** It does not publish, but correct it before landing.
- Acceptance note 3 says "each fetches only under a record context". That is false for `record:line_items` (see Census).
- H3 calls `DrillDownDrawer` "the drill list of the pivot, chart and metric blocks". The chart uses its own drawer, which mounts `object-data-table`, so the conclusion still stands.

### ② Semver level
- `@object-ui/plugin-tree`: patch. Correct.
- `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`: patch. Correct.
- Three blocks start re-reading on a bus that already exists. No published or authorable key, prop, export or type narrows. The extra list-view-tree read is a cost, not a surface change.
- Clause-② no is right for both packages. Never major: holds.

Among the successes: Test shards 1–8, Type Check, Lint, Build & E2E, Spec Main Shape Gate, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Claim Re-read and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Vercel status: success.

  - Against current main `6fa5f64a1d`: clean, tree `47000ae9da`. The PR's mergeable_state is `behind`.
